text:
sara: rolling out release/2026-03-batcher to canary now. small batcher change + buffer refactor. will watch latency panels.

deploy-bot: deploy started: release/2026-03-batcher -> canary (3 hosts)

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging eng-runtime on high tail latency in canary group (alerts: p95_token_latency > 600ms, error_rate spike)

mike: i’m on it, joining the canary dashboard. seeing p95 jump to ~1.2s and throughput drop on two hosts

sara: ack. what else? any 5xxs?

raj: 5xxs up ~3% on canary. logs show repeated KV cache misses + "kernel_fallback" traces in runtime logs on host canary-2

ellie: support seeing customer API errors for a handful of sessions, some returned 503s. capturing sample req ids now

mike: looking at runtime profiler — batcher is grouping requests into much larger micro-batches after buffer refactor. longer queueing, then eviction thrash on KV cache under memory pressure. that triggers fallback to slower kernels.

sara: so root _batch size growth_ -> memory spike -> kv eviction -> kernel fallback -> latency + 5xx. makes sense. is this caused by the new buffer window heuristic?

raj: yes, the heuristic bumped max_wait_ms from 5 -> 25 for “latency-tolerant” requests, which combined with sticky routing created big fanout batches.

ops-lead: recommend immediate safrollback of that flag for canary, and set max_wait_ms back to 5. we should revert config via feature flag rather than full image rollback if possible.

sara: agree. flipping release flag to restore old batcher behavior.

# command
```bash
redwoodctl feature flip --name=batcher_buffer_window --value=5 --scope=canary
```

deploy-bot: feature flip applied: batcher_buffer_window=5 (canary)

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Metric check: p95_token_latency dropping towards baseline on canary-1 and canary-3. canary-2 still high, investigating evicted kernel rollbacks.

mike: canary-2 appears to have persistent KV churn; restarting runtime on that host to clear stale caches.

# command
```bash
ssh canary-2 -- sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime
```

raj: restarted runtime on canary-2. KV cache warmup in progress. error_rate trending down.

ellie: CS: alerted impacted customers with tentative ETA 15m for full recovery. they reported some degraded tail latencies during morning traffic window.

sara: good call on flipping the flag. decision: do not full rollback image; propagate flag change to remaining canaries and stage rollout to prod only after bake at 1h and no regressions.

ops-lead: filing incident ticket and handing off to morning oncall for 1h bake and postmortem. action items: (1) revert buffer refactor PR to a branch for rework, (2) add limit on batch growth when server memory > 80%, (3) improve telemetry to correlate batch sizes -> kv eviction, (4) run load tests with sticky routing to catch fanout cases.

mike: noted. leaving runbook pinned in #eng-runtime. i’ll stay on for the handoff.

incident-bot: :page_facing_up: Incident created: INC-2026-03-XX - canary batcher buffer regression -> feature-flag revert applied. severity: high (customer-facing p95 spike, small subset affected).

ops-lead: handing off to morning oncall @raj for verification and postmortem writeup. thanks team :thumbsup:

sara: thx everyone, close thread when postmortem link is up.
